inputs: First expanded v2 image as style/detail reference
prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render.
Create the FINAL revised Tesoro map asset. Input 1 is a TECHNICAL SPATIAL PLAN; input 2 is the artwork STYLE/DETAIL reference. Follow input 1's WIDE FOUR-LOBED OUTER COMPOSITION precisely, render it richly using input 2's watercolor adventure-book style. This is essential: previous versions were too small after fitting the four-hex geometry. Do not reproduce the compact triangular island outline from image 2.
Canvas ratio 856:680, high resolution. Input 1's cream silhouette is the allowed footprint (a compact 2x2 hex union, bottom row shifted RIGHT). All dark blue outside must become fully transparent; cream gaps should mostly be filled with meaningful city, cliff or SHIPS, not water. Keep substantive content in all four lobes, including upper left houses up near that lobe's apex, lower left ships down near its apex, lower right house and ships out to its side and southern apex. There is an inset on the left halfway down: DO NOT extend cliffs/boats into that notch. A top central notch also stays empty. 10–15 diagram pixels safe margin inside the entire silhouette. Preserve the overall staggered broad shape, not a narrow diagonal strip. Nothing cut off; no final mask or hard polygonal edge. Organic edges of roofs, rocks, hulls and rigging naturally follow the plan.
Turn every schematic component into intricate, lovingly painted, plastic, colorful adventure-book scenery:
NW lobe: a substantial two-storey gateway tavern at west end, ladder down to short steep rock stairway, 2–3 more houses behind it on high grey timber platforms. No second city route bypassing the tavern.
Town spans from there across connected raised platforms and suspension bridges to the EAST and down the right-hand lobe, with two additional prominent houses lower right, hanging under-platform rooms, tall grey piles. Cool weathered silver-grey / blue-grey BUILDING planks, frames, doors, platform edges, supports and underrooms; warm golden windows; terracotta/ochre/teal roofs.
NE lobe: towering steep grey cliff immediately behind city, snowy peak and tiny snowy trail curling behind summit; small partly obscured lighthouse peeks from far side. Match reference mountain texture and subordinate lighthouse.
BOTH southern lobes: fill with a VERY DENSE broad carpet of chained ships, extending especially into lower LEFT and lower RIGHT, down to the two lower tips. Many large readable warm chestnut/copper/dark-walnut hulls, connecting planks, chains, masts and rigging, virtually no open navigable water. Few narrow aqua seams and foam only. Important material contrast: cool city timber versus warm ship timber.
Every ship sail is tightly FURLED: ivory cylindrical rolled cloth bundles on TOP of horizontal yards, tightly tied with 4–6 dark rope bands. NO draped scalloped cloth beneath yards, no open triangle sails and NO canvas sun canopies on decks. Diagram's short white bars with dark stripes represent these compact tied rolls.
Same oblique aerial viewpoint as reference, full continuous city in one connected image. No diagram colors, labels, boxes, geometric lines, border, words, watermark or background. True RGBA transparency. No square platform or exposed geometric cutout. Filling the four-lobed plan with actual detailed buildings and hulls is more important than preserving the reference's precise object positions.
